objective: Build the Kolibri Telegram Superfactory command layer: a human-language AI Telegram bot and modern Telegram Mini App integrated with the Kolibri Factory, Control Plane, Agent Host, Codex/MIMO/API runners, model/fleet status, task dispatch, task status, artifacts and owner memory. Use kolibriai.ru/frontend as the visual/product baseline where useful. First stabilize the runtime contract so only one canonical Telegram update receiver owns @kolibriai_bot; do not deploy a second poller. Implement as a server-side branch with tests, docs and safe deployment notes. Mac is only the dispatcher.

required_capabilities: Natural Russian owner dialogue grounded in factory context and project memory.
Owner can submit development, review, QA, DevOps and audit tasks from Telegram.
Owner can see fleet nodes, agent status, model status, active tasks, PR/CI summary and artifact links.
Bot routes tasks through Control Plane / Fabric API and never silently runs product work on Mac.
Bot can choose Codex, MIMO, API agents, local LLM, review agent or QA agent according to task type and policy.
Bot returns human-readable summaries instead of raw node ids, worktrees, logs or stack traces unless technical proof is explicitly requested.
Telegram Mini App provides modern mobile UI for command input, task board, nodes, models, artifacts, PR/CI and settings.
Mini App validates Telegram initData server-side before privileged reads/writes.
Runtime supports exactly one canonical update receiver: webhook preferred for production, polling only for emergency/bootstrap fallback.
Stale n8n/container/tmux/systemd Telegram pollers using the same bot token are detected and documented before any stop/disable action.
implementation_slices: Slice 0: finish or incorporate active Telegram poller diagnostic; leave primary gateway stopped until duplicate update receiver is resolved.
Slice 1: bot contract and docs: persona, context snapshot, memory, redaction, task routing, security gates and Mini App UX.
Slice 2: Telegram gateway runtime: single-owner update receiver, webhook-ready mode, health/status endpoint or runbook, clean owner-safe errors.
Slice 3: AI responder: factory-grounded prompt, project memory, active task awareness, no fixed canned greeting, no raw logs by default.
Slice 4: task dispatch: create Control Plane envelopes from Telegram commands/free text, choose target runner/node, track status and artifacts.
Slice 5: Mini App frontend: command composer, task board, fleet/model panels, artifact viewer, PR/CI cards, mobile Telegram-safe layout.
Slice 6: backend/Fabric endpoints: authenticated Mini App session validation, read-only status APIs, task submission bridge, artifact links.
Slice 7: tests and deployment runbook: unit tests, contract tests, frontend build/test where available, live smoke plan without exposing secrets.
verification_commands: if [ -f frontend/package.json ]; then (cd frontend && npm install --no-audit --no-fund && npm run build); fi
acceptance: All required docs and exact five run artifacts are created.
A server branch is created and pushed; no push to main and no force push.
The bot architecture is API-first and Control Plane/Fabric-integrated, not Mac-local.
Runtime guarantees one canonical Telegram update receiver; webhook/polling conflict handling is explicit.
No Telegram token, owner chat id, cookies, passwords, API keys or private messages are printed.
Mini App spec and/or implementation uses Telegram Web App initData validation and owner/admin authorization gates.
Owner dialogue is AI-generated from factory context and project memory, in Russian, human-readable, with no raw logs unless requested.
Task submission, status, artifacts, node/model status and PR/CI status are covered by contracts and tests.
MIMO/Codex/API/local LLM routing is represented as policy and code path where feasible, with broken runner auth reported instead of hidden.
Frontend/Mini App reuses Kolibri visual language from kolibriai.ru where practical and includes loading/error/empty/success states.
Telegram live deployment instructions include rollback and do not enable a second poller.
Remote result reports task ID, node, Russian agent display name, branch/PR, tests, blockers and next deployment command.
